output.brief: The 26-point gap mostly reflects who gets into Bridge Hours, not what the program does. District rules send every student below the 40th percentile on the fall test into it. Participants averaged 182.8 in the fall and non-participants 215.1, and 91% of participants were below the cutoff. Once students are matched on fall score, the gap shrinks to about 2 points or less, and it goes in both directions. Participants' faster growth (+15 vs +9) is also what you'd expect from low starters, so Northgate's claim isn't supported either. Students who scored below the cutoff gained 15.5 points whether or not they were in the program. This comparison can't detect a small effect either way. Don't end the contract on the raw chart, and don't expand it on the growth claim. Don't drop the referral list, because the state rule requires it. Next steps: put the matched comparison before the board in place of the raw chart, and ask the research office for the comparison of students just above and below the 196 cutoff (ready 27 Feb). Link attendance to scores, and have the math coordinator check the Stepwise fraction lessons, since teachers report a cross-multiplying conflict. Confidence is high that the raw gap is mostly selection. It is low on whether the program helps.
